Microarchitecture

Microarchitecture and memory addressing

How the Zynq system, the shared control unit and each processing element fit together, and the three addressing ideas that keep the memory simple.

System view

LinkZynq port / IPCarries
ARM → acceleratorM_AXI_GP0 → AXI Interconnect → AXI4-Lite slaveCSRs (μ, B, L, offsets, control), microprogram into IMEM, τ read-back
DDR → acceleratorAXI DMA (MM2S) on S_AXI_HP0 → AXI4-Stream64-bit beats: {mic4, mic3, mic2, mic1} × 16 bit
accelerator → ARMIRQ_F2P“τ ready”, level, cleared by writing STATUS.DONE

Vendor-neutral. The cluster only needs AXI4-Lite, AXI4-Stream, inferred RAM and inferred multiply-add. The DMA can be the Xilinx AXI DMA or the free Forencich verilog-axi core. A direct I²S microphone receiver could also feed the stream later, with no DDR involved.

C driver: load IMEM, write CSRs, set CTRL = IRQ_EN | AUTO | START. Per audio buffer, Xil_DCacheFlushRange (the HP ports are not cache-coherent), then XAxiDma_SimpleTransfer. The ISR reads TAU21/31/41, clears DONE and triangulates.

Control unit: fetch, decode, loops, AGU

The red “PC? instructions?” box in the week-2 draw.io is this unit. It is shared by all PEs because they execute the same instruction at the same time.

FetchPC + 2-entry loop stack {start, end, count}if PC = end and count > 1: next PC = start, with no bubble. There are no branches, so no branch penalty

AGUA0–A7, 13 bit + circular flagaddress = An; post-increment by IMM; circular = add in the low 9 bits only

Memory and addressing

① Reverse w, and both products read the same window

The golden model builds X[i] = x_full[i+L : i : -1], so X[i, j] = x_full[i+L−j]. Substitute k = L−1−j and store w_rev[k] = w[L−1−k]:

y[i]     = Σ_k x_full[i+1+k] · w_rev[k]      row i    = x_full[i+1 … i+L]
g_rev[k] = Σ_i x_full[k+1+i] · e[i]          column k = x_full[k+1 … k+B]
τ        = argmax_k |w_rev[k]| − (L−1−L/2)   = k* − 31

Both products now read ascending windows that start at x_full[1] and move one sample at a time. v1.0 read x and w ascending from x_full[0] and started column j at offset j. That still converges, but to a mirrored filter. Run on the same data, it reported +7 where the true delay was −7.

② The sliding-window register

WLD fills the window with aligned 16-sample chunks: 4 for Phase 1, 8 for Phase 3. After that, WSLIDE shifts it by one and pulls a single new sample from memory. Each row costs one memory read instead of four 16-wide loads.

Alternative considered: a rotator (16 × 16 crossbar of 32-bit words per read port) would allow a 16-wide load from any offset. That is the most LUT-hungry structure a PE could have, and it would be needed on every PE. The window register is 2 048 flip-flops plus an 8:1 chunk multiplexer, and the memory stays aligned-only.

③ Circular rings instead of copies and ping-pong buffers

input writer:  X_RING[(t + XOFF) mod 512] = mic(p+2)[t]     XOFF = L−1 = 63
               D_RING[(t + DOFF) mod 512] = mic1[t]         DOFF = L/2 = 32  (the center tap)
block n:       A7 = (n·B) mod 512   →  x_full[1] at X_RING+A7,  d_delayed[0] at D_RING+A7
  • The last 63 samples of block n are the first 63 of block n+1, already in place, so there is no history copy.
  • XOFF = 63 puts x_full[1] on a 16-word boundary, so every vector load is aligned.
  • While block n is processed (191 live words), the DMA writes block n+1 into the next 128 words. Before it could overwrite live data, the writer would have to be 321 samples (6.7 ms) past the end of block n. If that happens, TREADY drops (back-pressure) and STATUS.OVERRUN is set.
  • The D ring gets the center-tap delay for free through DOFF.

④ Banks and map

Word address a lives in bank a mod 16, row a / 16. An aligned vector access is one row across all 16 banks in one cycle. Scalar stores (y[i], g[k]) use that bank's write enable. The map (X ring 512, D ring 512, w_rev 64, y 128, e 128, g 64 words) uses 1 408 of the 8 192 words that 16 BRAM18s provide.

Most of the remaining cycles are stalls waiting for VREDUCE. Storing y[i−1] behind row i's VMACs (software pipelining) would cut Phase 1 to about 8 cycles per row. It isn't needed for real time.
